Explanation

Your application is trying to reach external resources via HTTP protocol.

For Managed Instance on App Service, secure connectivity to internal/on-prem HTTP services is managed via plan-level VNet integration and private endpoints. Keep inbound traffic restricted to 80/443; capture any required HTTP config in install scripts. Use Bastion JIT RDP only for diagnostics—persist all changes via install scripts. Outbound traffic does not impose similar restrictions.

While if targeting other Azure compute services, ensure the resources it is trying to reach are accessible from the Azure environment. If those HTTP requests are sent to internal services or services hosted on-prem, you probably will need to migrate those services to Azure as well.

Also, keep in mind that Azure App Service supports port 80 for HTTP and port 443 for HTTPS traffic. If you are using any other ports, you need to update them before moving to Azure.

Explanation

Synchronous API usage detected.

Using synchronous APIs can lead to more performance issues in Azure compared to on-premises environments due to different latency profiles. Consider adopting asynchronous code patterns.

In heavily loaded systems, especially where the I/O is substantial, using asynchronous patterns can improve overall throughput and performance. Asynchronous APIs enable a small pool of threads to manage thousands of concurrent requests without waiting on blocking calls. Instead of waiting for a long-running synchronous task to finish, the thread can handle another request. Conversely, numerous synchronous blocking calls can cause thread pool starvation and degrade response times.

Refer to the links below to learn more about asynchronous programming.

Architecture Diagram

eShopOnWeb is a sample online storefront with a server-rendered web application and a separate catalog/authentication API. The solution separates domain and application logic from ASP.NET Core presentation and Entity Framework Core infrastructure.

Data Storage & External Services

Catalog, basket, order, and identity data use SQL Server through separate catalog and identity contexts; an in-memory provider can be selected for testing or lightweight development. The web application also uses process-local memory caching for catalog view models. No message broker or external business API is configured in the inspected application.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • ApplicationCore owns business entities and service contracts; Infrastructure implements persistence with EF Core repositories.
  • The MVC storefront and PublicApi are separate ASP.NET Core projects in the same solution and share ApplicationCore and Infrastructure.
  • API authentication uses bearer JWTs, while the web application uses ASP.NET Core Identity/cookie authentication.

DTOs & Contracts

PublicApi contracts include AuthenticateRequest / AuthenticateResponse, CreateCatalogItemRequest / CreateCatalogItemResponse, UpdateCatalogItemRequest / UpdateCatalogItemResponse, CatalogItemDto, PagedCatalogItemResponse, CatalogBrandResponse, and CatalogTypeResponse. These are mutable DTO classes; no gateway-level aggregation model was found. Domain entities are persisted through the repository layer rather than exposed as a cross-service contract. JSON serialization uses System.Text.Json; Swagger/OpenAPI is generated with Swashbuckle.

Communication Patterns

BlazorAdmin makes synchronous HTTP calls to PublicApi using HttpClient. Web controllers and Razor Pages call application services directly in-process. PublicApi endpoints use application services/repositories and EF Core; no queue, event broker, service discovery, retry, circuit breaker, or client-side load balancing configuration was found. API catalog mutations require the administrator role and JWT bearer authentication; the authentication endpoint issues tokens. The storefront uses ASP.NET Core Identity authorization and HTTPS redirection. TLS is configured for local HTTPS profiles, while Docker development URLs use HTTP; no inter-service TLS policy was found.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. SQL Server starts before Web and PublicApi according to Docker Compose depends_on.
  2. Web and PublicApi initialize their EF Core contexts and seed catalog and identity data during startup.
  3. BlazorAdmin requires PublicApi availability for API-backed admin operations.
  4. No readiness health-check dependency or explicit wait-for mechanism was found in the Compose configuration.

Core Business Workflows

eShopOnWeb supports browsing a product catalog, managing a shopping basket, and placing orders through a sample storefront. Administrators maintain catalog data through a separate authenticated client and API.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Customer checkout

  1. An authenticated customer opens the basket and submits checkout.
  2. The Web checkout page loads the buyer's basket and applies submitted item quantities.
  3. OrderService loads the basket and its items, rejects a missing or empty basket, then loads catalog item details.
  4. The service builds order-item snapshots and an Order, then persists it through the repository.
  5. The basket is deleted after successful order creation and the customer is redirected to the success page.

Workflow 2: Catalog administration

  1. An administrator signs in and obtains a JWT from the authentication endpoint.
  2. BlazorAdmin calls catalog endpoints with the bearer token.
  3. API authorization restricts catalog create/update/delete operations to the administrator role.
  4. The endpoint applies catalog changes through repository operations. The current create behavior stores a placeholder image rather than accepting an uploaded file.

Cross-Service Data Flows

Web and PublicApi share the ApplicationCore and Infrastructure projects and access the same catalog persistence layer. The admin client receives API DTOs from PublicApi; no backend service aggregation or cross-service data composition pattern was identified. Checkout reads catalog details and basket state from the shared repository layer before writing the order.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Customer participant Checkout as "Checkout Page" participant BasketSvc as "BasketService" participant OrderSvc as "OrderService" participant Repo as "Repository" participant DB as "SQL Server" Customer->>Checkout: Submit basket quantities Checkout->>BasketSvc: Apply quantities BasketSvc->>Repo: Load and update basket Repo->>DB: Read/write basket DB-->>Repo: Basket with selected items Repo-->>BasketSvc: Updated basket BasketSvc-->>Checkout: Quantity update result Checkout->>OrderSvc: Create order for basket OrderSvc->>Repo: Load basket and catalog items Repo->>DB: Read basket and product details DB-->>Repo: Basket and catalog data Repo-->>OrderSvc: Basket with items and catalog items alt Basket has items OrderSvc->>OrderSvc: Create order and item snapshots OrderSvc->>Repo: Save order Repo->>DB: Persist order DB-->>Repo: Order saved Repo-->>OrderSvc: Success OrderSvc-->>Checkout: Order created Checkout->>BasketSvc: Delete submitted basket Checkout-->>Customer: Redirect to order success else Basket is empty OrderSvc-->>Checkout: EmptyBasketOnCheckoutException Checkout-->>Customer: Return to basket end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A checkout requires a non-empty basket; EmptyBasketOnCheckout rejects an empty selection.
  • Basket items for the same catalog item are combined by increasing quantity; zero-quantity items are removed.
  • Catalog item updates require non-empty name and description and a positive price.
  • Orders retain ordered item names, image references, and prices as purchase-time snapshots.
  • Checkout and order views require authentication; catalog mutation requires the administrator role.
  • Persistence operations are performed through scoped EF Core repositories. No distributed transaction or asynchronous event workflow was identified.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application stores catalog, basket, and order aggregates with Entity Framework Core, and stores users and roles through ASP.NET Core Identity. SQL Server is the configured persistent provider, with an in-memory provider option.

Caching Strategy

IMemoryCache is registered in the web and API hosts. Catalog view-model services use process-local caching for catalog listings and lookup data. No distributed cache, explicit cache TTL inventory, or second-level EF cache was found.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The catalog, basket, and order aggregates share the catalog database and CatalogContext; the identity model is isolated behind AppIdentityDbContext and its own connection setting. Web and PublicApi are separate hosts over shared application and persistence code, not independently owned microservice databases. Cross-domain operations use repository interfaces and in-process application services; there is no cross-service REST data join or CQRS read store identified.
